project.name: Application Hub
project.one_liner: A local web app that tracks US master's applications (deadlines, requirements, documents, interviews), manages recommenders in a sheet and drafts request emails, evaluates essays and CVs, and pushes reminders to a Google Calendar that syncs to the iPhone.

prerequisites: Claude Code, installed and signed in with your Claude subscription (`claude` works in a terminal)
Python 3 on PATH as `python` (for the hooks)
A Google account that is also added to the iPhone (Settings → Calendar → Accounts); needed from Phase 3

commands.setup: uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium

rules: **Never send email to anyone but the owner.** Request emails are copy-paste only; the only outbound email is the digest to `settings.owner_email`.
**Deadlines carry their time zone and source.** Every deadline is stored as a local time plus an IANA time zone plus a source URL; no code path drops either.
**Unverified stays visible.** Researched or third-party data is `unverified` until the user clicks Mark verified; never set `verified` in code or skills.
**Real data lives outside the repository.** Read and write user data only through the configured `data_dir`; fixtures and tests use invented people at example.com.
**Exact checks in code, judgement in the AI.** Word counts, wrong-school detection, deadlines and dates are computed in Python, never asked of the model.
**The AI comments, never rewrites.** Essay and CV feedback points at problems; it never produces replacement text.
**No invented facts in generated text.** Emails and feedback may only use facts present in the biography bank, the professor record or the programme data.

**Secrets stay unread.** Never open, print or copy `.secrets/` (OAuth client and token files) or paste their contents into the conversation; code reads them only at runtime through `config.google` paths.

decisions.decision: Python FastAPI with server-rendered Jinja templates and HTMX; no JavaScript framework
decisions.reason: One language, simple on Windows, enough for a single-user tool

decisions.decision: Data stored as YAML and Markdown files in a configurable data folder (OneDrive recommended)
decisions.reason: Readable and editable by the user and by Claude Code; OneDrive gives backup

decisions.decision: AI features call Claude Code (`claude -p`) with project skills on the user's subscription, not the API
decisions.reason: Single user; no API key; the same skills work interactively

decisions.decision: Reminders go to a dedicated Google Calendar 'Applications', reached on the iPhone through the Google account in iOS settings
decisions.reason: Reliable sync with alerts; subscriptions refresh slowly and may drop alerts

decisions.decision: Daily digest by Gmail API to the owner's own address, run by Windows Task Scheduler at login
decisions.reason: User choice; works without a server
User choice; Git gives per-phase checkpoints

decisions.decision: Berkeley Haas out of scope for now; addable through Add programme

limitations: Calendar sync and the digest only run while the laptop is on; events already on the phone keep their alerts.
Programme data is only as reliable as the user's verification against the source; admissions portals are not read.
AI feedback is diagnostic and not a prediction of what an admissions committee will think.
Button-triggered AI use draws on the subscription's separate Agent SDK credit.
CVs and essays are handled as pasted text; .docx and PDF import is out of scope.
model_note: Checked 30 Oct 2026: Claude Code offers effort levels from low to max. Use high effort for Phases 2b, 3 and 4b and for every planning and acceptance step; medium for the rest. Switch to a stronger model only if a phase keeps failing for reasoning reasons.

supervisor.user_style: Direct, confident and specific; recommendation first; accuracy over embellishment; formal register for anything sent to professors.
environment_notes: Windows native with VS Code; uv for Python
Claude Code runs on the user's Claude subscription
